newsitem.title: HONG KONG: FOCUS - HK's Hang Seng back above 13,000 points.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - HK's Hang Seng back above 13,000 points.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index shot above the 13,000 point level for the first time since mid-March on Thursday, but while momentum seemed to be gathering steam, analysts said it was too early to say if it could be sustained.
The blue chip index jumped 117.48 points, or 0.91 percent, to close at 13,020.78 on Thursday, extending a 302.88 point gain registered on Wednesday.
"This is a very strong rally which has been underway and it is largely backed by Wall Street and the long bond yield," said Andrew Fernow, director of research at Vickers Ballas.

The Dow industrials staged their second-largest point gain ever on Tuesday, rising 179.01 points. The move was followed by a 46.96 point gain on Wednesday to 7,008.99, bringing the Dow above 7,000 points for the first time in nearly seven weeks.
Fears that the U.S. Federal Reserve may raise interest rates at its May 20 meeting were soothed this week following the release of softer-than-expected wage inflation data.
The improvement in sentiment pushed the U.S. long bond yield below the seven percent level and the yield on the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond stood at 6.96 percent on Wednesday.
"The long bond yield has fallen to less than seven percent so this gives a lot of relief to investors on interest rates," said Peter So, deputy head of research at Schroder Securities.
"If the trend continues, there probably will be more momentum in the market, especially in the property stocks."
But analysts said with Friday's U.S. April employment report still hanging over the market, Hong Kong stocks still had a major hurdle to cross.
"All it will take is more data to scare us away in terms of the next Federal Reserve meeting," said Fernow.
"There could be some data that could convince investors to be prepared for another rate hike and that could crimp the momentum that we have seen lately."
Delta Asia Securities senior research manager Ricky Tam said the Hang Seng Index was likely to consolidate between 12,800 points and 13,000 points in coming days.

"On Friday the U.S. will release employment data so this will keep the market from moving higher. I think in the recent rally the market moved a bit too fast so some profit-taking may take place around 13,000," he said.
Weakess in HSBC Holdings Plc shares, which ended Thursday down HK$1.00 at HK$195.00 (US$25.17) despite the Hang Seng's move upwards, could also hold the index back.
But Tam said the Hang Seng could then resume its uptrend, with a recent move above 12,800 points possibly signalling the end of a consolidation period.
"Turnover for the blue chips is a bit heavy. It is quite a good sign," he added.
